content.title: About
content.content: Abalone is a marine mollusk from the family Haliotidae. It lives in cold coastal waters of the Pacific and Indian Oceans. The flesh is prized for its delicate, slightly sweet flavor and firm yet tender texture. It is commonly used in sushi, salads, pastas, and as a gourmet appetizer.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Abalone shells have a pearly interior that is harvested for mother‑of‑pearl jewelry and decorative items.
In Japan it is called “uni‑ko,” and in China “hai‑shou,” and is considered a lucky delicacy.
These mollusks can live up to 30 years and reach lengths over 30 cm.
There are more than 100 species, but Haliotis discus and Haliotis laevigata are most commonly eaten.
Harvesting is regulated in most countries to prevent over‑exploitation.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Abalone provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, making it a good source of complete protein.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many seafoods, abalone is low in fat, most of which are healthy polyunsaturated fatty acids.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: It contains iron, zinc, magnesium and calcium, supporting blood health, bones and nervous system.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Abalone supplies vitamin B12 and B6, important for metabolism and nerve function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Shell pigments such as carotenoids have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Mollusks can accumulate cadmium and lead; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Possible parasites
items.content: Raw or undercooked abalone may contain parasites; cook to at least 70 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Abalone is often served lightly seared, baked, or as sashimi. Slice thinly for salads, add to pasta, soups, or prepare in a buttery sauce. Before cooking, remove the shell and rinse the meat under cold water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh abalone in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C, wrapped in a damp cloth, for up to 2 days. Frozen abalone can be stored in an airtight bag for up to 3 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Canned apricots are whole apricot fruits (Prunus armeniaca) that have been pitted, cooked in a sweet syrup, and sealed in glass or metal jars. They retain the fruit's delicate flavor, soft flesh, and bright orange color, while preserving most of the vitamins and minerals found in fresh apricots.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Apricots belong to the Rosaceae family and are closely related to peaches, plums, and cherries.
Canning extends the shelf life of apricots to 2–3 years without major loss of taste.
Traditional recipes use a syrup with added citric acid to keep the vivid color.
In Japan, apricots are sometimes canned in a soy‑based glaze for sweet‑savory dishes.
High beta‑carotene content makes apricots a good source of provitamin A.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A
items.content: Apricots provide beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain fluid balance and normal heart function.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Flavonoids and vitamin C protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Skin health support
items.content: Vitamin A and vitamin C contribute to skin renewal and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Canned apricots are often packed in sweet syrup, so they should be consumed in moderation, especially by people with diabetes.

items.title: Apricot allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to severe symptoms.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain brands may add food preservatives; check the label if you are sensitive.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic syrup can irritate the stomach in people with high gastric acidity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned apricots can be enjoyed as a snack, added to yogurt, oatmeal, baked goods, salads, or used in sauces for meat. They also work well in smoothies and ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5–7 days.

infant-formula-enfamil-prosobee-powder-m.title: Infant formula, Enfamil ProSobee, powder, made with baby water

content.title: About
content.content: Enfamil ProSobee is a hypoallergenic infant formula powder designed for newborns and infants with heightened sensitivity to cow‑milk proteins. It contains a fermented lactose hydrolysate, prebiotics, DHA, and specially processed baby water, providing easy digestion and a minimal risk of allergic reactions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: ProSobee was the first hypoallergenic formula in the Enfamil line to undergo clinical trials for reducing the risk of atopic dermatitis.
The formula includes the prebiotic GOS (galacto‑oligosaccharides) that supports the development of beneficial gut microbiota in infants.
DHA (docosahexaenoic acid) is added to promote brain and visual development.
Preparation uses specially filtered and sterilized baby water that meets strict purity standards.
Each container yields approximately 400 ml of ready‑to‑feed formula, making it convenient for travel.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Hypoallergenic proteins and prebiotics help strengthen the infant’s immune system and lower the chance of food allergies.

items.title: Brain development
items.content: DHA supports neuronal growth and visual function during critical periods of development.

items.title: Easy digestion
items.content: Hydrolyzed lactose protein is easier for the infant’s gastrointestinal tract to process.

items.title: Balanced nutrition
items.content: The formula provides an optimal balance of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals needed for growth.

items.title: Gut microbiota support
items.content: GOS prebiotics promote the growth of beneficial bacteria, improving digestive health.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Although hypoallergenic, some infants may still react to trace milk proteins.

items.title: Improper reconstitution
items.content: A solution that is too concentrated can strain an infant’s kidneys; always follow the manufacturer’s mixing instructions.

items.title: Storage after opening
items.content: Opened containers should be refrigerated and used within 48 hours to prevent bacterial growth.

items.title: Lactose content
items.content: The formula contains lactose; infants with lactose intolerance should be evaluated by a pediatrician.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Measure the recommended amount of powder, add sterile baby water at 37 °C, and stir thoroughly until smooth. Let the mixture stand for 2–3 minutes, then check the temperature before feeding.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dry powder in its original airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated and use within 30 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Mojito is a refreshing Cuban cocktail made with white rum, fresh lime juice, mint, sugar (or simple syrup), and sparkling water. It features a bright citrus flavor, aromatic mint, and a light sweetness, making it a popular summer drink.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recorded recipe appeared in the early 19th century and was called “El Draque.”
Traditionally the mint leaves are gently muddled to release essential oils, not pulverized.
The original version used dark rum, but today light rum is more common.
Mojitos are usually served in tall highball glasses with ice to keep them cold.
Variations often add strawberries or other berries for extra flavor.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Lime juice is rich in vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Refreshing effect
items.content: Mint and sparkling water help quench thirst and can ease mild nausea.

items.title: Low calorie count
items.content: When made with moderate sugar, mojito contains fewer calories than many sweet cocktails.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Mint is traditionally used to aid digestion and relieve spasms.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: Mojito contains rum, so it is not suitable for children, pregnant women, or those avoiding alcohol.

items.title: Sugar
items.content: High amounts of sugar can raise blood glucose levels; consider using simple syrup or a substitute.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Lime increases the drink’s acidity, which may irritate sensitive teeth or the stomach.

content.title: How to Make
content.content: Place 6–8 mint leaves, 2 teaspoons of sugar, and the juice of half a lime in a glass. Gently muddle the mint to release aroma. Add ice, 50 ml white rum, top with sparkling water, and stir lightly. Garnish with a sprig of mint and a lime wedge.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Mojito is best served immediately. If you need to store it, keep it in the refrigerator for no more than 2 hours, and store mint and lime separately to preserve their freshness.

nutritional-drink-or-shake-ready-to-drin.title: Nutritional drink or shake, ready-to-drink (Carnation Instant Breakfast)

content.title: About
content.content: Carnation Instant Breakfast is a ready‑to‑drink nutritional shake designed as a quick breakfast. It provides milk protein, vitamins, minerals, and carbohydrates for energy. The product comes in several flavors and can be enjoyed cold or warmed.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first ready‑to‑drink breakfast appeared in the United States in the 1960s.
It is widely used by the military and expedition teams because of its long shelf life without refrigeration.
The formula includes fermented milk proteins that aid rapid absorption.
A sugar‑free version is available for those monitoring calorie intake.
In some markets the product is sold as a powder for reconstitution, but the original version is ready to drink.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2, B6 and B12 support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Help maintain healthy bones and teeth, especially when dairy intake is low.

items.title: Contains milk‑derived protein
items.content: Provides a quick supply of amino acids after waking, aiding muscle recovery.

items.title: Carbohydrates for fast energy
items.content: Includes simple and complex carbs that raise blood glucose promptly.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Supports normal blood formation and helps prevent fatigue.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: The product contains dairy protein, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Some flavors contain added sugar, which may be unsuitable for diabetics or those watching weight.

items.title: Lactose content
items.content: People with lactose intolerance should choose lactose‑free versions or alternative drinks.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Those monitoring salt intake should be aware of the sodium amount per serving.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Consume the shake straight from the bottle, chilled in the refrigerator or at room temperature. Ice, fruit, or protein powder can be added for flavor variety and extra nutrition.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 7‑10 days.

rice-brown-with-vegetables-cheese-and-or.title: Brown Rice with Vegetables and Cheese/Cream Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice with vegetables and a cheese or cream‑based sauce is a nutritious dish featuring whole grain rice, assorted vegetables, and a smooth sauce made from cheese and/or cream. It provides complex carbohydrates, fiber, B‑vitamins, minerals, and a moderate amount of fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains the bran and germ, giving it more nutrients than white rice.
Typical vegetables include carrots, broccoli, bell pepper and peas, boosting vitamins A, C and K.
Cheese/cream sauce is often prepared with low‑fat cheese or reduced‑fat cream to keep it creamy without excess calories.
The dish is popular in Asian and Mediterranean cuisines as a light lunch or dinner.
Brown rice has a lower glycemic index than white rice, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: The bran in brown rice supports digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B3 and B6 aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Vegetables and cheese sauce provide vitamin C and polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Calcium from cheese and magnesium from rice contribute to strong bones.

items.title: Moderate fat content
items.content: A sauce made with low‑fat dairy supplies essential fatty acids without excessive calories.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese and cream can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces may be salty; people monitoring sodium should control portion size.

items.title: Carbohydrate load
items.content: Brown rice still contains a notable amount of carbs; diabetics should watch serving sizes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main meal or side. It pairs well with chicken, fish or tofu for extra protein. Add fresh herbs or a squeeze of lemon for brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When reheating, add a splash of water or broth to prevent the sauce from drying out.

content.title: About
content.content: Roll "White Soft" (item 2416) is a delicate bread roll made from wheat flour, milk, butter and a touch of sugar. It has a soft, airy crumb and a mild sweet note, making it perfect for breakfasts, snacks, and as a base for various fillings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White soft rolls are commonly used in traditional Eastern European dishes such as open‑face sandwiches and canapés.
The dough is usually given a proofing period, which creates the characteristic porous texture.
The original recipe uses butter rather than vegetable oils, giving it a distinctive aroma.
When kept in a sealed package, the rolls stay fresh for 3–5 days at room temperature.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The roll provides a quick source of energy thanks to easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, which support metabolism.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Milk and butter add a modest amount of calcium beneficial for bones.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The roll contains wheat flour and is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Because of its simple carbs, the roll can raise blood sugar levels quickly.

items.title: Sugar and fat content
items.content: For those monitoring weight, moderate consumption is advised due to added sugar and butter.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: White soft rolls can be eaten fresh, sliced and spread with butter, jam, cream cheese, or used as a base for sandwiches with ham, cheese, and vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store rolls in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 5 days. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator (up to 10 days) or freeze (up to 3 months). Allow them to come to room temperature before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Fried scallops are a seafood product made from bivalve mollusks of the family Pectinidae. Scallops have a delicate, slightly sweet flavor and a firm yet tender texture. When fried they develop a golden crust while retaining their juiciness and the taste of the sea.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Scallops can grow rapidly; some species double their weight in just a few weeks.
In the wild scallops filter water, helping to clean their environment.
Scallops have been part of the human diet for over 10,000 years, making them one of the oldest seafood staples.
Frying scallops is often accompanied by garlic, butter, and herbs, which enhance their aroma.
Scallops contain hemoglobin, giving their flesh a characteristic pinkish hue.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Scallops provide complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Mineral source
items.content: Scallops are a good source of zinc, selenium and iron, important for immunity and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many seafood items, fried scallops contain relatively little saturated fat when cooked with moderate oil.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Scallops provide EPA and DHA, which promote heart and brain health.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to scallops, ranging from mild symptoms to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Toxin contamination
items.content: Scallops can accumulate toxins (e.g., domoic acid) in polluted waters; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Over‑cooking
items.content: Excessive frying makes scallops tough and may create harmful compounds.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Scallops contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried scallops are served hot as an appetizer or incorporated into dishes such as salads, pastas, and rice bowls. Squeeze lemon juice over them, add fresh herbs, garlic, or a splash of soy sauce for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fried scallops in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a sealed bag, removing as much air as possible.
